proposedGenericDecision: Refer to the dominant-suite vendor's enterprise-licensing renewal cycle in role terms (the incumbent productivity/identity-suite vendor and its periodic licensing-renewal milestone), so the trajectory describes the structural fact (procurement organised around a recurring vendor-renewal cadence) without binding to one named vendor.
rationale: Microsoft is the most common but not universal incumbent. The structural point (sovereignty grid integrated into a procurement practice driven by a recurring enterprise-licensing renewal milestone) generalises cleanly to any dominant-suite vendor (e.g., Google Workspace, regional suites). Naming Microsoft fixes the document to one vendor environment.

surfaceForm: the documentation of Microsoft estate components, their contractual envelopes, and their data flows
proposedGenericDecision: Refer to the incumbent dominant-suite estate components rather than 'Microsoft estate components'; the inventory task is to document the dominant vendor's estate, contractual envelopes and data flows whatever that vendor is.
rationale: Same vendor-binding as above; the inventory description is generic once 'Microsoft' is replaced by the incumbent-suite role.

surfaceForm: more involved than in the Microsoft-centric trajectory
proposedGenericDecision: Replace the back-reference 'Microsoft-centric trajectory' with the role-based name of the single-incumbent brownfield trajectory (e.g. 'the dominant-suite brownfield trajectory').
rationale: Cross-reference inherits the vendor name from the section title; must be generalized consistently with the section rename.

proposedGenericDecision: Rename the trajectory to a role-based label such as 'brownfield single-dominant-suite' or 'brownfield incumbent-suite'; keep Microsoft only as an illustrative example inside the body, not as the trajectory's identity.
rationale: The trajectory taxonomy (greenfield / single-incumbent brownfield / hybrid brownfield) is structurally vendor-neutral; encoding 'Microsoft' into the taxonomy label makes the whole playbook scaffold vendor-bound.

surfaceForm: For the most common European starting point
proposedGenericDecision: Replace the region-bound qualifier 'European' with a region-neutral framing ('the most common brownfield starting point for institutions with an established single-vendor productivity/identity suite'), or parameterize the region if the playbook is to be localized per region.
rationale: Asserts a regional prevalence claim (European) without it being intrinsic to the trajectory. Implicit assumption that the adopting institution sits in the European market; an institution-agnostic / region-agnostic playbook should not hard-code the region.

surfaceForm: principal anchor of NIS2 Art. 20 (management-body accountability for security measures and training)
proposedGenericDecision: Treat NIS2 as the EU-jurisdiction instance of a 'management-body cyber-accountability obligation' role; for an institution-agnostic playbook, parameterize the binding instrument (and its national transposition) so non-EU adopters bind to their equivalent management-accountability regime, with NIS2 Art. 20 given as the EU example.
suggestedLocalizationVariable: MGMT_ACCOUNTABILITY_INSTRUMENT (EU default: NIS2 Art. 20 + national transposition)
rationale: NIS2 is an EU directive requiring national transposition; citing it as the 'principal anchor' silently assumes EU jurisdiction and a national transposition the country of which is unnamed. The governance principle (management-body accountability) is universal; the binding instrument is jurisdiction-specific.

surfaceForm: \gls{gdpr} Art. 24 (controller responsibility) when read at institutional level
proposedGenericDecision: Keep GDPR Art. 24 as the EU/EEA instance of the data-controller-accountability role, but mark it as jurisdiction-conditional so non-EU adopters substitute their data-protection regime (e.g., national DP law) as the equivalent anchor.
rationale: GDPR binds EU/EEA controllers; presenting it as the controller-responsibility anchor assumes EU jurisdiction. The accountability principle generalises; the named regulation does not.

surfaceForm: NIS2 Art. 21(2)(d) (supply-chain security) operationalised more fully at Wave 9
proposedGenericDecision: Same as the NIS2 Art. 20 treatment: present the supply-chain-security obligation as a role (binding supply-chain-security duty) with NIS2 Art. 21(2)(d) as the EU instance, parameterized for non-EU jurisdictions.
rationale: EU-directive citation carries the same unstated-jurisdiction / unnamed-national-transposition assumption as the other NIS2 reference.

surfaceForm: MIT's Information Technology Governance Committee (ITGC), reporting to the Provost and Executive Vice President, with related committees on infrastructure, policy, and projects
proposedGenericDecision: Keep as an illustrative, clearly-labelled external precedent (the box already says the adopting institution should pick precedents resonating with its own framework). It is role-illustrative, not a self-reference, so retention is acceptable; if strict neutrality is desired, demote to a generic pattern ('a provost-level IT governance committee with subsidiary committees on infrastructure, policy and projects').
rationale: This is a third-party exemplar inside a realworldbox explicitly framed as 'identify the precedents that resonate with your own framework', not a claim about the adopting institution. It supports rather than fixes institution-identity. Flagged for awareness; the 'Provost and Executive Vice President' governance shape is US-specific and could mislead readers into assuming that governance topology.

surfaceForm: central University Information Services (UIS) at Cambridge supporting a collegiate model that combines central and college-level IT arrangements
proposedGenericDecision: Same disposition as the MIT precedent: retain as a labelled external exemplar of a 'collegiate / federated central+unit IT model', optionally demoting to a generic pattern description if strict neutrality is required.
rationale: Third-party exemplar, not a self-reference; the box already instructs the adopter to substitute its own precedents. The 'collegiate model' governance shape is Cambridge/Oxford-specific and should remain clearly illustrative.

surfaceForm: Patterns reported in NREN community fora and in EDUCAUSE publications
proposedGenericDecision: EDUCAUSE (US/HE) and NREN fora are sector-consensus sources; acceptable to keep as evidence sources, but consider neutral phrasing ('NREN community fora and higher-education IT professional-body publications') so the document does not implicitly privilege the US/EU sector-body landscape.
rationale: These are legitimate Layer-3 sector-consensus sources, not institution self-identity. Mild regional flavor (EDUCAUSE = North American HE association) but used as evidence, not as a binding assumption. Low priority for genericization.

surfaceForm: an IT Council adds the sovereignty grid to its agenda; a procurement committee adopts grid-based gating clauses
proposedGenericDecision: These are offered as examples ('e.g.') of existing bodies and are already generic role-names (IT Council, procurement committee) rather than a named institution's organs. Keep; they describe generic governance organs, not a specific rectorate/board-of-governors topology.
rationale: 'IT Council' and 'procurement committee' are generic governance-body archetypes presented as illustrations, not an assumed single governance topology. No rectorate/board-of-governors shape is hard-coded. Listed for completeness; no change needed.

surfaceForm: indicatively the equivalent of one to two engineer-years over the wave's duration
proposedGenericDecision: The cost is already expressed as a jurisdiction-neutral FTE proxy (engineer-years) rather than EUR, which is the correct generic form. Keep as-is; optionally parameterize the FTE band if regional sizing guidance is desired.
rationale: Engineer-years is deliberately currency- and jurisdiction-agnostic, avoiding the EUR-bound cost anti-pattern. The band (1-2 engineer-years) is a sizing heuristic, not a UL-specific figure. Retain; flagged only as an optional localization knob.
